change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: unsubscribe raises a 500 error when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when no row exists, and line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, which raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. The mailer creates a row only for the email's recipient (`TopicUser.change` at app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:312, which inserts when no row is found, app/models/topic_user.rb:97-106). Any other logged-in account that opens the link has no row for that topic and gets an error page. That covers a forwarded email, a browser logged in to a different account, or anyone typing `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never visited. Fix: if `tu` is nil, call `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: muted)`, or treat it as the default level (column default 1 = regular, topic_user.rb:341).

findings.title: Each GET lowers the level by one step, so a reload or a second click mutes the topic
findings.body: The action does not set a fixed level. Each request lowers the current one: above regular goes to regular, otherwise to muted (lines 107-111). The first click moves a watching user to regular. Reloading the page, clicking the email link again, or using browser Back/Forward into a fresh page load moves them on to muted. A muted topic is dropped from their topic lists, and nothing on the page says this happened: the page always shows the same "You will stop receiving notifications" text. Choose one target level, for example muted, or only lower the level when it is still the one the email was sent for. Then repeated requests are idempotent.

findings.title: A plain GET changes state with no CSRF protection, so any site can change a user's notification level
findings.body: The route is a GET (config/routes.rb:440-441) and `check_xhr` is skipped for it (line 32). Every other notification-level change in this controller is a PUT/POST protected by the CSRF token (`set_notifications`, `mute`, routes.rb:450,473). Here, any third-party page or forum post can embed ``. The browser then sends the victim's session cookie, and the topic is silently changed to regular, or to muted on a repeated load (see the finding on line 107). Options: carry a signed per-user/per-topic key in the email link, as the digest unsubscribe does with `email_unsubscribe_url(key: ...)` (app/views/user_notifications/digest.html.erb:76), or render a confirmation page and make the change with a POST.

findings.title: A logged-out user who clicks the email link lands on the home page and is not unsubscribed
findings.body: `unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. For an HTML GET from a logged-out user, `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` is handled with `redirect_to path("/")` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:100-103). People often open email links in a browser where they are not logged in. They end up on the home page with no login prompt and no message, the unsubscribe never happens, and they are not sent back to it after logging in. A signed token in the link (see the CSRF finding) would avoid needing a session at all. Failing that, redirect to login with a return path.

findings.title: The page says notifications stop, but watching and tracking users only drop to regular
findings.body: The page always shows "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". But the controller moves any level above regular (watching or tracking) only to regular (topics_controller.rb:107-108). At regular, the user still gets reply, mention and quote notifications and their emails. For a tracking user the first click changes almost nothing about emails. So the user is told something false and keeps receiving the emails they asked to stop. Either mute directly, or word the message to match the level actually set, e.g. use the new level's name.

findings.title: Typo in property name `stopNotificiationsText`
findings.body: "Notificiations" is misspelled here and in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3. Consider renaming to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.

findings.title: No test covers the new unsubscribe action or the per-topic link
findings.body: The spec change only passes `unsubscribe_url`, so the I18n interpolation does not fail. Nothing asserts that the body/HTML contains the per-topic link. There is also no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: level transitions, a missing TopicUser, slug redirect, logged-out user. The nil and repeated-request bugs above would have been caught by such tests.

contracts.action: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes the current user's TopicUser.notification_level and renders the topic show page
contracts.equivalent_path: TopicsController#set_notifications / mute via PUT/POST (config/routes.rb:450,473), which go through TopicUser.change and publish a MessageBus notification_level_change
contracts.before_after: Before: no GET path changed notification level. After: each GET lowers the level by one step (watching/tracking→regular, regular→muted) via tu.save!, bypassing TopicUser.change, so no notifications_changed_at/reason_id update and no MessageBus publish
contracts.visible_effect: perform_show_response stores the preloaded topic JSON and renders :show; the Ember topicUnsubscribe route then shows the stop-notifications text and the notifications dropdown
contracts.failure_mode: tu nil → NoMethodError 500; logged-out → redirect to '/', no unsubscribe; repeated loads mute the topic silently

contracts.action: Notification emails include a per-topic unsubscribe link
contracts.before_after: Before: unsubscribe_link interpolated only user_preferences_url. After: it also needs unsubscribe_url; the only caller with add_unsubscribe_link: true (send_notification_email) supplies it as an absolute URL from Topic#url
contracts.visible_effect: Text body appends the link; the HTML footer gets cooked markdown through %{unsubscribe_link}
contracts.failure_mode: A caller with add_unsubscribe_link and no unsubscribe_url would raise an I18n missing-interpolation error; no such caller exists today

contracts.action: Client route topicUnsubscribe loads the topic and hides the notification reason text
contracts.before_after: Loads /t/:id.json with topics#show, not the unsubscribe action, so client-side navigation or Back to this route does not repeat the level change; it sets details.notificationReasonText to null on the record
contracts.visible_effect: Renders the stop-notifications text and a topic-notifications-button whose longDescription (an alias of notificationReasonText) is now empty
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected loadTopicView has no error handling in this route and falls to Ember's default error route. Not confirmed: whether store.createRecord shares the topic instance with the regular topic route, which would leave the reason text null there
contracts.open_question: Does store.createRecord('topic') return a cached identity-mapped instance shared with the topic route, so that nulling notificationReasonText leaks there?

contracts.action: dropdown-button omits the title <h4> when no title is given
contracts.equivalent_path: All dropdown-button subclasses (notifications-button defaults title to '')
contracts.before_after: Before: always pushed an <h4> (possibly empty or 'undefined'). After: only when title is truthy
contracts.visible_effect: Buttons with an empty title lose the empty heading

summary: The PR adds a per-topic unsubscribe link to notification emails. The email side works: the only caller that adds an unsubscribe link now also passes the new topic URL. The server action has several problems: (1) it returns a 500 error when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic; (2) every GET lowers the notification level one step, so reloading or clicking twice mutes the topic without telling the user; (3) it changes state on a GET without CSRF protection, unlike the existing PUT/POST notification endpoints; (4) a logged-out user is redirected to the home page and is never unsubscribed. The page also says notifications will stop when watching and tracking users only drop to regular, where they still get reply and mention emails. There are no tests for the new action.
